breath_title: It's the environment, not the checklist.
breath_text: Applicants aren't ranking program attributes; they're choosing a learning environment where they hope to grow. That same theme runs through this week: clinical teachers who feel judged by student evaluations that miss their world, a call for a shared vocabulary so coaching can be studied, and new reviews on belonging and on what it means when students feel unmotivated.

top.headline: Interview season check: applicants are choosing a learning environment, not a feature list
bullets: Scoping review of 65 studies (2015-June 2026, US/Canada) in 41 journals; 95.4% were surveys, mostly author-built.
1,237 selection factors (about 19 per study), mapped to a Learning Environment framework: social 25.6%, organizational 25.3%, personal 24.7%, societal 20.6%.
Physical and virtual space factors were rarely studied (2.4%).
top.tip: audit your interview day by domain. Do applicants see the social and organizational culture (residents, feedback, support), or just the rotation schedule?
top.citation: Perez NA, Martinez AM, Means C, Hall E, Costello JA, Gilbert E, Maggio LA. Acad Med. Online Nov 7, 2026. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag351

top.headline: "This is just not their world": clinical teachers on student evaluations of teaching
bullets: Toronto Department of Medicine interviews: 10 faculty leaders and 15 frontline clinical teachers across subspecialties.
Clinical workload and relationships with learners shaped how faculty experienced SETs; many felt departments didn't respond to their concerns, leaving them isolated and undervalued.
Many doubted SETs were fair or useful for high-stakes decisions without safeguards. Suggested alternatives: peer review, third-party observation, and credit for mentoring and curriculum work.
top.tip: if learner evaluations feed promotion files, pair them with direct observation or peer review and tell faculty how the data are used.
top.citation: Lee C, Chandran N, Dhamko H, Bui E, McDonald-Blumer H, Brydges R. Med Teach. Online Nov 11, 2026. doi:10.1080/0142159X.2026.2756415

top.headline: Coach, mentor, advisor, therapist? A shared dictionary for coaching programs
bullets: A Scholarly Perspective from the CHARM Coaching Network proposes standard definitions across 5 dimensions: coaching format, modality, type, framework, and focus.
Separates professional (developmental) coaching from mentoring, advising, and therapy that use a "coach approach."
Describes the core coaching process and the difference between coach training, certification, credentialing, and accreditation.
top.tip: before you launch or evaluate a resident coaching program, write down which kind of coaching it is, using these terms, so your outcomes can be compared.
top.citation: de Guillebon E, Dyne P, Caylor T, Pendo A, Berliner J, Sikon A, Palamara K. Acad Med. Online Nov 10, 2026. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag353

quick.text: AAP policy: pediatric workforce diversity. Three focus areas: grow the URiM pipeline, improve recruitment, retention, and leadership development of URiM pediatricians, and advance culturally effective care (Ndjatou T et al.; Section on Pediatric Trainees co-author. Pediatrics. Online Nov 9, 2026).

Clerkship absence policies. IM clerkship director survey: 116/140 schools (83.0%); 81% have a list of approvable absences. Authors urge simpler lists and in-person make-up time (Fitzpatrick JH et al. Acad Med. Online Nov 2, 2026).

Belonging for URiM students. Scoping review of 41 sources (39 since 2020): barriers, costs like masking and overperformance, and institutional fixes. Make belonging an outcome (Lim JJ et al. Adv Health Sci Educ. Online Nov 11, 2026).

"Useless, too much, no one cares." 16 pre-clinical students drew and discussed feeling unmotivated: boredom and overwhelm turned learning transactional (Schipper SA et al. Med Educ. Online Nov 10, 2026).
